title: Children's data - the special obligations companies must follow
p1:
A child clicking “accept” on an app may not understand what they are agreeing to. But the company collecting that data is expected to know better.

Children's personal information is not treated like ordinary user data.
p2:
Many businesses assume that if a child can use a service, they can collect their information the same way as adults. That is a costly misconception.

Companies often face stricter rules when handling children's data because children may not fully understand privacy risks or how their information could be used.
p3:
The real obligation is not just collecting less data. Companies may need clearer explanations, stronger safeguards, parental involvement in some situations, and careful limits on how children's information is shared or used.

A simple rule: the younger the user, the greater the responsibility.

Privacy design is no longer only about compliance. It is about protecting people who may not know they need protection.
conclusion: Should companies face stricter accountability when collecting data from children, even if parents allow their use of the service?
